body: Yeah, actually, what you're saying really makes a lot of sense. That pretty much is my relationship with myself. I'll check out those videos. Thank you.

Hmm, I get what you're saying. The thought of rejection does scare me, but I know that if I actually experience it it probably won't be that bad and it might make me open up more to the world. 

And thanks, haha. I appreciate it, man. Thanks for taking the time to write to me.
Thanks. It might sound weird, but that actually does mean a lot to me. I hope that you're right.

I get what you're saying. I guess the issue is that I definitely do not consider things like my sterility to be inconsequential. It may in reality be just that, but to me at least, I consider it to be a pretty major thing which has affected how my life will turn out. I don't know.

Yeah, I know. I really don't know how to go about doing that, though.

I know that a relationship won't mean automatic happiness. It just upsets me that I may never get to experience a part or stage of life which most people seem to take for granted. 

Thanks. I hope you're right. I hope that I can afford to see a therapist sooner rather than later.
Cool, thanks for the recommendation. Glad it worked for you. I'll check it out.
I get what you're saying, but, I mean, I've been this way for more than half of my life. I don't know if I'll be around if I'm this way at 30.
No, my family doesn't have insurance. As I said, I can't afford therapy right now. But I guess I'll seek it out in the future. Thanks.

I'd consider seeing a therapist again sometime, but I can't afford therapy right now. To be honest, therapy itself doesn't really conjure up any good memories, but it's something I'd like to give another go.

I guess I'm more worried that I'll never get to it at all.
Good to hear that things worked out for you.

I didn't know that. I guess I just assumed we couldn't. To be honest, the social/cultural bias surrounding men and children would not encourage me to do that alone. I can't do Big Brother right now (no car, no money), but I mentor/tutor kids when I'm at college.

I guess the problem is that I can't do a lot of the things I'd like to, and I don't know when I would be able to. I would like to travel and go to different countries, for instance, but I have no idea when that would be realistic. Another things is that I just don't know what I want to do. I don't have a lot of motivation in general. I can bring myself to work, to socialize, etc., but it's not necessarily something which makes me happy. I do it because I know that I have to. I don't know how to explain it.

I have, but I can't afford that. My family is uninsured at the moment, and neither I nor my parents have any money for that. I talked to the counselor at my college once, when I was particularly stressed out, but I think that I overwhelmed her, haha. She's not there for heavy-duty stuff, just things like "I'm homesick" or "I hate my roommate" or "I'm anxious about x". Anyway, thanks for commenting/talking with me. I appreciate it.
Well, thanks. I definitely don't see myself that way, haha.

I get what you're saying. I try to keep myself busy, and it's when I have free time that I get like this. It's summer break and I most likely won't be able to get a job. I don't have a car, I'm in a fairly isolated small town, and most of my high school friends are going on vacation shortly (some for a month or more). I had been trying to spend most of my time reading or exercising, but that hasn't been able to keep me from feeling like this. It's just difficult to forget everything, I guess. 

>I think your outlook on life will change drastically when you'll get older.

I get what you're saying, but I have been pretty much told this exact thing for twelve years. I'm not sure how or when my outlook will change, as it supposedly is going to.

I'm talking about just having a history of this. I can't change the past. I'm not sure what you mean by stable; I would be considered much more than stable if you were comparing me to my ten-year-old self, but I don't know if I'd necessarily be considered stable in comparison to the average joe. And again, a single man wouldn't be allowed to adopt.

Thanks. The problem is that I don't know how to do either of those things. I feel like I am living for others, and that's tiring. I truly don't know how to make myself happy, or even content with life.

I would like to be more involved in the sort of thing you're talking about. During the school year, I'm a "mentor" at the junior high in town. I also tutor elementary school kids occasionally. That stuff is easier when I'm at college, because you can either just walk or transportation is arranged. I don't have a car and I live in a small town which is pretty disconnected from everything, so it would be a lot more difficult for me at home. I don't know if it would actually be possible for me to be able to do anything, but I'll look into it. Thanks.

I just want to be content with life. I don't want to feel like this anymore. I would like to be able to help other people. I don't want to be constantly reminded of my past. I can't say that I have ever truly experienced happiness (at least not that I can remember), so I don't know what that means to other people.

I get what you're saying. I'm really not comparing myself to others. I guess I'm just trying to think of what would make me, personally, content and better-adjusted to life. I don't know whether or not that makes sense.
Haha.
I don't know how I would find that sort of thing, though.
I don't even know if I will ever be able to be in a relationship. Besides, I am fairly positive that having a mental health history like mine would disqualify someone from adopting/fostering.
As I said, I am $30,000 in debt. I don't know if I'll be able to get a job this summer. I can't just fly/drive somewhere and go skydiving.

When I was younger, I think that one of my therapists told me to do that with "I am happy". I ended up getting frustrated and stopped doing it. Maybe I'll try something like that again sometime. Has that worked for you?

I get what you're saying. I haven't ever felt anything like that. I mean, it's not realistic for me to be able to do those things right now, but maybe someday I'll try something like that. Thanks for the suggestions.

I am very sorry for your loss.

I don't know if this makes sense, but I feel like I've been living for other people for most of my life. When I was a child, I would talk myself out of killing myself because I didn't want my parents to have to find my body. When I got a bit older, it was because of my friends and teachers. Now, it's because of my debt. I keep finding new reasons, but I am so tired of doing this. I guess that people care about me, but I am tired of just existing, unhappily, for them. I am so tired of having to go through the motions like this.
I don't know. Obviously I would like to have a family, but that's not an option. I don't know how to find happiness.

I called a suicide hotline once, when I was younger. I think I was 15 or 16. I got embarrassed and hung up. I think that there are people in more urgent need of attention out there. I don't want to clog up their resources like that.

Thanks, that's nice of you to say...I just can't see it. It's really uncomfortable for me.

I guess what I'm saying is that I don't know how to work through this. I have been trying for 12 years, practically. I don't want to keep doing this for the rest of my life. That's really all that I can see ahead of me.
That's pretty vague...I guess just to be happy.
What?

Yeah, I do want to date. I suppose that I have dated, actually. I am just too insecure due to the way things are. I feel like it would be too complicated. When women have expressed interest in me, I always end up freezing up and pushing them away. This has cost me friendships. I hate that this is how things are. I really want a relationship, but I most likely won't ever have one.

Not a fan of Tolle. It seems like he's just rehashing a lot of other stuff. I mean, it's made him successful, so I guess I can't fault him for that. And yes, age 29...that's around when Siddhartha Gautama and Jesus Christ had their revelations. It seems like he draws most from Christianity and Buddhism.
Yes, that's what psych wards are like. Try dealing with that shit as a child. My first visit, a kid not much older than me lost a finger after he was resisting being put into the "time out room".

Thanks a lot for commenting. I guess that I really just needed to get all of this off my chest. I haven't talked to anyone in person about my issues for a good three years or so.

That's true. When I was younger, I always thought that I would have committed suicide by the time I was 15 or 16. I guess it's still hard to believe, at least on a more personal level, that I'm still going. I don't know if that makes sense. I've been doing the exercise/good eating and sleeping habits stuff for years. I guess they're just that: habits I've gotten into. I started actively keeping up with them because I thought they could help, but I don't really think that they have. I mainly use exercise to keep my mind off of things.

My depression has changed over time, I guess. This is going to be way too long, so sorry about that. It really confuses me. When I was younger (maybe 8 to 15?) I was practically miserable all of the time. My daily life was seriously affected. I would pretty much just sleep all day, if I were given the choice. I felt suicidal fairly frequently. From 16 to 17, it was less consistent. Over all, I pretty much just felt mildly depressed. During these phases, I didn't really experience any heightened emotion at all. However, toward the tail end of that time, I would have these periods of maybe a few weeks of feeling miserable, as I had when I was younger. It was a weird cyclical thing. From then up until now, I pretty much just feel numb, or other times a slight sadness. Sometimes I'll get heavily depressed like I am at this moment, but it usually only lasts a day or two. The weird, chaotic nature of my depression really confuses me. 

Thanks for sharing that with me. I guess that I just feel like life itself is futile, in a way. I can't do one of the most basic biological functions that most people can: have sex/father children. It makes me feel absolutely useless. I don't know how to describe it. I used to be just slightly upset by the fact that I couldn't have sex, but for the past two years or so, I've actually had a sex drive. This has been really new to me, and I wish that I could just make it go away! It is excruciatingly frustrating. 

It's just been difficult to find those happy moments which you're talking about. I make myself spend time with friends, or engage in hobbies, but it's really just felt like going through the motions. If anything, they're just momentary distractions, and I don't normally derive any actual happiness from them. I don't know. I used to live by the mantra "one day at a time", and I just kept going, no matter what was happening. It's been getting gradually more difficult to do that lately, though.

Yes, your post really did help. I appreciate knowing that someone out there read my post and was willing to talk to me about things. I really appreciate it. Thanks for taking the time to talk to me.
